newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn coalition agrees surcharge cut in '98-sources.
newsitem.headline: Bonn coalition agrees surcharge cut in '98-sources.

text.p: The leaders of Germany's three-party ruling alliance have agreed to cut an income tax surcharge next year even if broad tax reforms fail to clear parliament, coalition sources said on Tuesday.

Junior coalition partners the Free Democrats (FDP) had demanded a cut in the solidarity surcharge by two points to 5.5 percent, and sources in Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democratic Union (CDU) said they had agreed to the move.
"Our intention is clear," one coalition source said.

The FDP has pressed to cut the "soli" -- an unpopular levy raised to finance economic regeneration in eastern Germany -- through a separate law if Finance Minister Theo Waigel's plan to slash 30 billion marks in tax is blocked in parliament.
The reduction would cost the government around seven billion marks. It remained unclear how the lost revenues would be covered but the sources said ideas for this were being considered.
Bonn is under heavy pressure to control borrowing both this year and next to keep its budget deficit and qualify for Europe's single currency.
